name: Relay Brief

scoring.report_note: Report individual before/after deltas and the team's average shift. Never rank people by how much they dropped — the relay loses information at every hop by design; the point is the pattern, not a culprit.

description: Two-minute pre/post measure for Relay Brief. Scores how a team's habit of checking instructions changes after they watch a five-constraint brief degrade across four hops: retention, clarifying before acting, assumption-injection (reverse), rebuild fidelity and single-source confidence (reverse).

instructions.pre: Before the relay. Each participant answers alone, about how handovers went in their own last week — not about the game.
instructions.post: Right after the reveal and debrief. Same items, now answered about what the relay just showed them.

items.pre_text: When something is passed to me verbally, I catch all of the constraints.
items.post_text: Seeing the brief shrink hop to hop showed me how much a verbal handover really loses.

items.pre_text: Before acting on an instruction, I restate it back to the person who gave it.
items.post_text: After the relay, I want to restate a brief back before I act on it.

items.pre_text: When an instruction is unclear, I fill the gap with what seems obvious and move on.
items.post_text: The relay proved how each hop quietly fills gaps with guesses.

items.pre_text: I can rebuild a task's requirements from memory well enough to act on them.
items.post_text: The final rebuild proved how little survives memory across even four hands.

items.pre_text: I trust that one clear telling of a brief is enough — no need to write it down.
items.post_text: The relay made me want the brief in writing, not one voice down a line.

report.title: Relay Brief — handover-discipline delta
sections: Hop-by-hop fidelity loss (the constraint score at each hop)
One written-handover habit the team commits to, from the biggest positive delta
